body.statement:
For every \(N\geq1\) and \(g\geq0\), the joint orientation frontier is finite, is nondecreasing in each argument, and satisfies
\[
 \vartheta_{N,g}\leq\min\{2^g,\tau_N\}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\qquad\text{whenever }N\geq2g+1.
\]
For five available vertices the exact finite recurrence values are
\[
 (\vartheta_{5,g})_{g=0}^{6}=(1,2,4,6,8,12,24),
 \qquad
 \vartheta_{5,g}=24\quad(g\geq6).
\]
body.proof_tex:
For a fixed connected simple graph \(H\), choosing \(X_i\) from the factor indexed by \(\{i,j\}\) is the same as orienting that edge toward \(i\).  Consequently \(c_H(r)\) is exactly the number of orientations of \(H\) with indegree vector \(r\).  Only finitely many labeled simple graphs on at most \(N\) vertices and finitely many orientations of each graph occur, so the maximum defining \(\vartheta_{N,g}\) is finite.  Enlarging \(N\) or \(g\) enlarges the feasible collection, proving monotonicity.

Fix a spanning tree \(S\) of \(H\), and write \(b=|V(H)|\).  There are
\[
 |E(H)\setminus E(S)|=|E(H)|-(b-1)=g(H)
\]
non-tree edges.  For a prescribed indegree vector \(r\), fix orientations of those \(g(H)\) edges.  There is at most one compatible orientation of \(S\): at a leaf of the current tree, the required residual indegree forces the orientation of its unique remaining tree edge, after which that leaf may be deleted; induction on the number of vertices proves uniqueness.  Therefore
\[
 c_H(r)\leq2^{g(H)}\leq2^g.
\tag{1}
\]
The established fixed-edge completion in \(\mathrm{lem:tournament\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}fiber\mbox{-}ceiling}\) also gives \(c_H(r)\leq\tau_N\) whenever \(b\leq N\).  Taking the maximum over \(H,r\) proves
\[
 \vartheta_{N,g}\leq\min\{2^g,\tau_N\}.
\tag{2}
\]

For the reverse inequality in the stated range, first let \(g=0\).  The included one-vertex graph gives \(\vartheta_{N,0}\geq1=2^0\), which combines with (1).  Now let \(g\geq1\).  Form a bouquet of \(g\) triangles by taking a central vertex \(z\), two new vertices \(u_i,v_i\) for each \(1\leq i\leq g\), and the three edges
\[
 \{z,u_i\},\quad\{u_i,v_i\},\quad\{v_i,z\}
\]
for each \(i\).  This connected simple graph has \(2g+1\) vertices, \(3g\) edges, and hence cyclomatic number
\[
 3g-(2g+1)+1=g.
\]
Orient each triangle as either of its two directed cycles.  Every such choice has indegree \(g\) at \(z\) and indegree one at every \(u_i,v_i\).  The choices are independent across triangles, so for
\[
 r_z=g,\qquad r_{u_i}=r_{v_i}=1
\]
the score fiber contains \(2^g\) orientations.  Thus \(\vartheta_{N,g}\geq2^g\) when \(N\geq2g+1\), and (1) proves equality.

For completeness, the five-vertex values are certified by the following finite coefficient recurrence.  Given a labeled graph \(H\) with lexicographically ordered edges \(e_j=\{u_j,v_j\}\), define
\[
 A_{H,0}(r)=\mathbf 1\{r=0\},
 \qquad
 A_{H,j}(r)=A_{H,j-1}(r-\mathbf e_{u_j})
             +A_{H,j-1}(r-\mathbf e_{v_j}),
\tag{3}
\]
where a term with a negative coordinate is zero.  Expanding one factor at a time proves by induction that
\[
 A_{H,|E(H)|}(r)=c_H(r).
\tag{4}
\]
Put \(\mu(H)=\max_r c_H(r)\), and let \(N_{b,m}(s)\) be the number of connected labeled graphs on \([b]\) with \(m\) edges and \(\mu(H)=s\).  Applying the additions in (3) to every subset of the at most ten possible edges gives the following complete audit table; within a row, \(N(s)\) abbreviates \(N_{b,m}(s)\), and a blank entry is zero:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|l|c}
b&m&\{s:N_{b,m}(s)\ne0\}&\sum_sN_{b,m}(s)\\ \hline
1&0&N(1)=1&1\\
2&1&N(1)=1&1\\
3&2&N(1)=3&3\\
3&3&N(2)=1&1\\
4&3&N(1)=16&16\\
4&4&N(2)=15&15\\
4&5&N(3)=6&6\\
4&6&N(4)=1&1\\
5&4&N(1)=125&125\\
5&5&N(2)=222&222\\
5&6&N(3)=190,\ N(4)=15&205\\
5&7&N(4)=50,\ N(5)=60,\ N(6)=10&120\\
5&8&N(7)=15,\ N(8)=30&45\\
5&9&N(12)=10&10\\
5&10&N(24)=1&1
\end{array}
\tag{5}
\]
This table is independently checkable without graph-isomorphism choices: scan the edge subsets in lexicographic order, reject a subset unless a search from vertex \(1\) reaches all \(b\) vertices, and use (3).  As an arithmetic checksum, if \(a_{b,m}=\sum_sN_{b,m}(s)\), decomposition by the connected component containing vertex \(1\) gives
\[
 a_{1,0}=1,
 \qquad
 a_{b,m}=\binom{\binom b2}{m}
 -\sum_{q=1}^{b-1}\binom{b-1}{q-1}
   \sum_{\ell=0}^{m}a_{q,\ell}
   \binom{\binom{b-q}{2}}{m-\ell}.
\tag{6}
\]
Substitution in (6) gives exactly the last column of (5).

The maxima in the seven five-vertex rows are attained explicitly.  Let
\[
 S=\{12,13,14,15\},
\]
and, for \(0\leq h\leq6\), let \(H_h\) have edge set \(S\cup A_h\), where the following table also gives a score vector whose coefficient is maximal:
\[
\begin{array}{c|l|c|c}
h&A_h&r&c_{H_h}(r)\\ \hline
0&\varnothing&(4,0,0,0,0)&1\\
1&\{23\}&(3,1,1,0,0)&2\\
2&\{25,34\}&(2,1,1,1,1)&4\\
3&\{23,24,25\}&(2,2,1,1,1)&6\\
4&\{23,24,25,34\}&(2,2,2,1,1)&8\\
5&\{23,24,25,34,35\}&(2,2,2,2,1)&12\\
6&\{23,24,25,34,35,45\}&(2,2,2,2,2)&24
\end{array}
\tag{7}
\]
Each coefficient in (7) follows by the same seven-or-fewer applications of (3) after the four star edges have been processed.  Since a connected graph with \(b\) vertices and \(m\) edges has cyclomatic number \(m-b+1\), (5) supplies the upper bounds and (7) supplies matching lower bounds for every \(0\leq g\leq6\).  Hence
\[
 (\vartheta_{5,g})_{g=0}^{6}=(1,2,4,6,8,12,24).
\]
Finally a simple graph on at most five vertices has cyclomatic number at most
\[
 \binom52-5+1=6.
\]
Thus increasing \(g\) beyond six adds no feasible graph, and \(\vartheta_{5,g}=24\) for every \(g\geq6\).
